summary: California APSA regulates facilities with aggregate aboveground petroleum storage capacity at or above 1,320 gallons (with containers under 55 gallons generally excluded from counting). The proposed change identifies only 60 gallons of flammable solvent. Even if the solvent is petroleum, one 60-gallon container is far below the 1,320-gallon APSA threshold. Therefore APSA is not expected to apply on the stated facts, but the determination is conditional because the facility’s total aggregate aboveground petroleum storage capacity and whether the solvent is petroleum were not provided.
title: H-HAZMAT-APSA: 60 gallons of solvent at coating shop is not enough to trigger California APSA unless additional petroleum storage exists
